title: Drowsy Cache Lines
constraints: An 8-line data array (8 bits per line). Each line is either awake or **drowsy** (low retention voltage: data kept but not accessible). `drowsy[i]` shows line i's state.

An access (`req`) is resolved on the rising edge with a registered result. If the line is awake: `ready <= 1`, and a read loads `rdata`, a write updates the line. If it is drowsy: `ready <= 0`, no data operation, the line wakes up and `wakeups` increments (the requester retries). Without `req`, `ready <= 0`.

A free-running 4-bit window counter wraps every 16 cycles. On the edge where it wraps (count 15 → 0), **all** lines become drowsy. An access on that same edge is still resolved using the pre-edge state.
Synchronous reset: all lines drowsy, data 0, counters 0, `ready = 0`.
hints: The drowsy mask update on each edge: `drowsy <= wrap ? 8'hFF : (drowsy & ~wake_bit)`.
`rdata` only needs to be valid when `ready = 1` after a read.
This 'simple' policy (Flautner et al., ISCA 2002) cuts L1 leakage a lot, because most lines aren't touched within a few thousand cycles.
